queryPrefix: Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages:

pages.title: 4ocean
pages.desc: 4ocean removes plastic from oceans, rivers, and coastlines with full-time cleanup crews, funded by products made from recovered plastic.

pages.title: ALOS-4 "DAICHI-4" (JAXA)
pages.desc: JAXA's DAICHI-4 radar sees through clouds over a 200 km swath, continuing the radar record used for deforestation alerts.

pages.title: Start Here: AP Physics and IB Physics Topic Map
pages.desc: Free physics, orbit and aeronautics math pages, labs and calculators matched to AP Physics 1, 2 and C: Mechanics units and IB Physics topics, with sources.

pages.title: ATLAS Asteroid Terrestrial-impact Last Alert System
pages.desc: Four robotic telescopes, two in Hawaiʻi, search the entire dark sky every 24 hours for asteroids that could hit Earth, so people can be warned.

pages.title: About
pages.desc: How Saving Planets picks practical, sourced solutions for oceans, lakes, rivers, forests and space, and how you can suggest one. Positive action, not panic.

pages.title: Aditya-L1 (ISRO)
pages.desc: Aditya-L1 is ISRO's first space-based solar observatory, studying the Sun from a halo orbit around L1, about 1.5 million km from Earth.

pages.title: Aeolus Assisted Reentry (ESA)
pages.desc: ESA guided its retired Aeolus wind satellite down in the first assisted reentry of its kind, cutting the already low debris risk by a factor of 150.

pages.title: How Flight Works
pages.desc: Flight explained for kids, teens and college students: lift, weight, thrust and drag, wings, the atmosphere, jet engines, helicopters and stability.

pages.title: Aero Lab
pages.desc: Interactive Aero Lab: ISA stall-speed calculator, short-period eigenvalue plotter with flying-qualities check, and rotor hover-power slider, in 5 languages.

pages.title: Aeronautical Engineering Math, Step by Step
pages.desc: Atmosphere, lift, wings, performance, shocks, jet engines, stability and rotors: derivations, worked examples and practice, freshman to PhD.

pages.title: Adopt-a-Beach (Alliance for the Great Lakes)
pages.desc: Each year, Adopt-a-Beach volunteers remove tens of thousands of pounds of litter from Great Lakes beaches, about 85% of it plastic.

pages.title: Amazing Facts That Matter
pages.desc: Surprising, sourced numbers behind ocean cleanup, rivers, replanting, space and orbital computing. Every fact keeps its source and is free to reuse with a link.

pages.title: The Amazon Makes Its Own Rainy Season
pages.desc: Water breathed out by Amazon trees starts the rainy season two to three months before winds alone would bring it (NASA JPL).

pages.title: American Forests
pages.desc: Since 1875, American Forests has worked to restore U.S. forests, from big natural landscapes to city streets, with more than 63 million trees planted.

pages.title: American Rivers
pages.desc: American Rivers has worked directly on more than 200 dam removals; in 2025 the U.S. removed 100 dams and reconnected more than 4,893 river miles.

pages.title: Arbor Day Foundation
pages.desc: Since 1972, the Arbor Day Foundation says it has planted more than half a billion trees, working in more than 60 countries (nonprofit figures).

pages.title: Argo Ocean Float Array
pages.desc: Close to 4,000 robotic floats dive through the ocean and send back temperature and salinity data, free to everyone. The 3 millionth profile came in 2024.

pages.title: Argos Satellite Tracking System
pages.desc: A satellite system that tracks wildlife and ocean instruments from tiny transmitters, following more than 8,000 animals every month for conservation science.

pages.title: Ariel Exoplanet Mission (ESA)
pages.desc: ESA's Ariel will study the atmospheres of a thousand planets orbiting other stars, revealing what they are made of (ESA).

pages.title: Artemis Program
pages.desc: NASA's Artemis program: Artemis I flew in 2022, Artemis II carried four astronauts 252,756 miles from Earth in April 2026, and Artemis III is targeted for 2027.

pages.title: Astroscale
pages.desc: Astroscale inspects, services and removes debris in orbit: ELSA-d, ADRAS-J's 2024 close-up of an H-IIA upper stage, and ADRAS-J2, targeted for fiscal 2027.

pages.title: Atmospheric Drag
pages.desc: Atmospheric drag is Earth's natural space debris removal: it pulls low-orbit junk down to burn up, faster when the Sun is active, but barely works up high.

pages.title: Beavers, River Engineers
pages.desc: In Oregon's Bridge Creek, beavers given simple dam starters raised juvenile steelhead survival 52% and production 175% (NOAA Fisheries).

pages.title: BepiColombo (ESA / JAXA)
pages.desc: After eight years in space, BepiColombo enters orbit around Mercury on 21 November 2026, the first mission to put two spacecraft there (ESA).

pages.title: Billion Oyster Project
pages.desc: A New York nonprofit restoring the harbor with oyster reefs, aiming for one billion oysters by 2030 (nonprofit figures).

pages.title: Biomass (ESA)
pages.desc: ESA's Biomass satellite, launched April 29, 2025, carries the first P-band radar in space, seeing through forest canopies to measure the carbon stored in trees.

pages.title: Launch Your Name: Boarding Pass
pages.desc: Kids make a free printable keepsake boarding pass for the next real rocket launch. Made on your device: your name is never saved or sent.

pages.title: Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS)
pages.desc: Europe's air monitoring service forecasts air pollution, smoke and dust worldwide twice a day for more than 23,500 users, free and open.

pages.title: CHIME Hyperspectral Imaging Mission (ESA)
pages.desc: CHIME will image Earth in more than 200 colours of light to support sustainable farming, food security and biodiversity (ESA).

pages.title: CIMR Copernicus Imaging Microwave Radiometer (ESA)
pages.desc: Two Copernicus satellites will measure sea ice, sea-surface temperature and salinity over 95% of the globe every day, with sub-daily polar views (ESA).

pages.title: Copernicus CO2M Carbon Dioxide Monitoring (ESA / EU)
pages.desc: A planned trio of satellites that will measure the carbon dioxide and methane people release, so countries can check whether their emission cuts are working.

pages.title: CRISTAL Polar Ice and Snow Altimeter (ESA)
pages.desc: CRISTAL will carry the first dual-frequency radar altimeter to measure polar sea-ice thickness and the snow on top, following ESA's CryoSat (ESA).

pages.title: Start Here: JROTC and Civil Air Patrol Aerospace Topics
pages.desc: Free pages, labs and calculators matched to the aerospace topics in public JROTC course descriptions and in Civil Air Patrol aerospace education modules.

pages.title: Aerospace & Physics Calculators
pages.desc: Free, fast calculators for delta-v, Hohmann transfers, orbital period and velocity, stall speed, lift, Mach number, thrust-to-weight, hover power and pendulums.

pages.title: Aerospace, Space and Earth-Science Careers: Pay, Outlook and How to Get There
pages.desc: What aerospace engineers, pilots, A&P mechanics, drone pilots, physicists and space operators do, the path from high school, and official U.S. pay data.

pages.title: Carruthers Geocorona Observatory (NASA)
pages.desc: The first mission dedicated to Earth's exosphere, Carruthers watches our planet's ultraviolet halo from about a million miles sunward.

pages.title: Catalina Sky Survey
pages.desc: A NASA-funded survey in Arizona that has discovered more near-Earth objects than any other: 17,918 near-Earth asteroids since 1995.

pages.title: Changelog: what is new on Saving Planets
pages.desc: Every solution added to Saving Planets, newest first, with the date it was added. Each batch is dated by the day it was released, so you can see what is new.

pages.title: Chesapeake Bay Foundation
pages.desc: Since 1966, the Chesapeake Bay Foundation has worked to save the Bay and its rivers, adding more than 21 million oysters in fiscal year 2026 (CBF).

pages.title: Clean Lakes Alliance (Madison, Wisconsin)
pages.desc: Clean Lakes Alliance works to improve water quality in Madison's Yahara lakes; it reports 81 monitoring stations and over $1.4 million in grants (its figures).

pages.title: Clean Up the Lake
pages.desc: Clean Up the Lake removes submerged litter from freshwater lakes using scuba divers and volunteers, and GPS-pins, sorts and weighs every piece it finds.

pages.title: ClearSpace
pages.desc: ClearSpace leads Europe's first active debris removal mission and provides in-orbit servicing. It is a privately held in-orbit servicing company.

pages.title: Comet Interceptor (ESA / JAXA)
pages.desc: Three spacecraft will wait in space for a fresh comet and fly past it together to make a 3D map; launch is planned for late 2028 or early 2029 (ESA).

pages.title: Contact
pages.desc: Send us a solution, an idea or a question. Email ideas@savingplanets.com with the next page, story or fix you think Saving Planets should cover.

pages.title: Copernicus Emergency Management Service: On-Demand Mapping
pages.desc: The European Union's emergency mapping service turns satellite images into maps for disaster teams, 24/7 since 2012, with more than 1,000 activations.

pages.title: Copernicus Marine Service
pages.desc: Free, open ocean data and forecasts for the whole planet. In 2025 users downloaded almost 15,000 terabytes of ocean data from Copernicus Marine.

pages.title: Coral Gardeners
pages.desc: Coral Gardeners grows corals in nurseries and replants them on reefs in French Polynesia, Fiji and Thailand: 238,250 corals planted so far.

pages.title: Coral IVF (Great Barrier Reef Foundation)
pages.desc: Researchers capture coral spawn and rear millions of baby corals for damaged reefs; the first Coral IVF corals reproduced on the Great Barrier Reef in 2021.

pages.title: Coral Reef Watch (NOAA)
pages.desc: NOAA's Coral Reef Watch uses satellites to warn of the ocean heat that bleaches corals, with daily monitoring of 95% of the world's coral reefs.

pages.title: Coral Restoration Foundation
pages.desc: Coral Restoration Foundation had returned 253,833 corals to Florida's reefs by the end of 2024 (organization figure). Florida's Coral Reef in the Florida Keys.

pages.title: Coral Vita Land-Based Coral Farms
pages.desc: Coral Vita grows reef-building corals on land up to 50 times faster than in nature, and says it has grown over 100,000 corals (company figures).

pages.title: Corrections
pages.desc: Spot a mistake on Saving Planets? Tell us what is wrong using the short form on this page and we will fix it fast, in every language.

pages.title: CryoSat Ice Mission (ESA)
pages.desc: CryoSat measures polar sea ice and the great ice sheets from space, and its data revealed 85 hidden lakes under Antarctica (ESA).

pages.title: DSCOVR / EPIC (NASA–NOAA)
pages.desc: NASA's EPIC camera rides on NOAA's DSCOVR spacecraft at the L1 point, photographing the entire sunlit face of Earth several times a day, with an archive...

pages.title: Forests
pages.desc: Forest solutions: three trees for every one removed, native biodiverse reforestation, and large-scale European planting.

pages.title: Delta-v Calculator (Tsiolkovsky Rocket Equation)
pages.desc: Delta-v is how much a rocket can change its speed by burning its propellant. Ideal rocket: no gravity or drag losses, constant exhaust speed.

pages.title: Dragonfly Titan Rotorcraft (NASA)
pages.desc: NASA's Dragonfly is a car-size rotorcraft that will fly across Saturn's moon Titan to study the chemistry that came before life (NASA).

pages.title: European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS)
pages.desc: Europe's wildfire system forecasts fire danger and maps burnt areas from satellites. In 2024 it mapped wildfires in 42 countries.

pages.title: EMIT (NASA)
pages.desc: NASA's EMIT instrument on the International Space Station maps the minerals in desert dust and has spotted methane super-emitters from space (NASA JPL).

pages.title: EOS-06 / Oceansat-3 (ISRO)
pages.desc: India's EOS-06, the third Oceansat, tracks ocean color, sea-surface temperature and winds; it imaged Cyclone Mandous and an algal bloom on day one.

pages.title: Near-Earth Object Coordination Centre (ESA)
pages.desc: Europe's asteroid watch centre computes orbits and impact risks every day and keeps a public list of every asteroid with a non-zero chance of hitting Earth.

pages.title: ESCAPADE (NASA)
pages.desc: NASA's twin ESCAPADE spacecraft will study how the solar wind strips Mars' atmosphere, after an Earth slingshot in fall 2026.

pages.title: EarthCARE (ESA–JAXA)
pages.desc: ESA–JAXA EarthCARE carries the first space cloud radar that can measure how cloud particles move up and down, sharpening forecasts of how clouds affect climate.

pages.title: Earth Observation
pages.desc: Earth Observation solutions: NASA-ISRO NISAR, ESA Biomass, Tanager-1 methane detection and DSCOVR EPIC, measuring land, forests, leaks and ozone.

pages.title: Eden: People+Planet
pages.desc: Eden: People+Planet restores landscapes with local communities, including a 394,000-hectare project in Tanzania's Rubeho Mountains (Eden).

pages.title: Editorial & Sources Policy
pages.desc: How we choose solutions, check facts and use SI. Each number links to where it came from. Organization claims are labeled as the organization’s own figures.

pages.title: Elwha River Restoration
pages.desc: Two Elwha River dams came down between 2011 and 2014, and more than 20 million tons of trapped sediment flowed downstream to rebuild the river and coast.

pages.title: EnVision (ESA)
pages.desc: ESA's EnVision will study Venus from its inner core to its upper atmosphere, and may show how a planet like ours got so hot. Launch is planned for late 2031.

pages.title: Enceladus
pages.desc: Saturn’s small moon Enceladus hides a global ocean and sprays it into space. Cassini found water, salts, organics, hydrogen and phosphates there.

pages.title: Europa Clipper (NASA)
pages.desc: NASA's Europa Clipper is on its way to Jupiter's ocean moon, with an Earth gravity assist on December 3, 2026 and 49 close Europa flybys from 2030.

pages.title: ExoMars Rosalind Franklin Rover (ESA)
pages.desc: Europe's first Mars rover, Rosalind Franklin, will drill 2 meters down to look for signs of past life, targeting launch in 2028.

pages.title: FIRMS Fire Information for Resource Management System (NASA)
pages.desc: NASA's FIRMS delivers satellite fire detections within 3 hours anywhere on Earth, and in real time for the US and Canada. Free for firefighters and everyone.

pages.title: FLEX and Sentinel-3C (ESA)
pages.desc: Launched together on September 15, 2026, ESA's FLEX maps the faint glow of photosynthesis while Sentinel-3C watches oceans and land.

pages.title: FORUM Far-Infrared Mission (ESA)
pages.desc: ESA's FORUM will measure Earth's outgoing far-infrared radiation, never measured from space before, filling a missing piece of the climate jigsaw (ESA).

pages.title: Find a Cleanup
pages.desc: Find a beach, river or lake cleanup near you. Official cleanup event finders, sorted by region. We don't run cleanups or keep our own list of events.

pages.title: FireSat (Earth Fire Alliance)
pages.desc: Earth Fire Alliance's FireSat satellites are built to spot wildfires as small as 5 by 5 meters from space and get the data to firefighters fast.

pages.title: Forest Elephants, Carbon Gardeners
pages.desc: By thinning small trees, forest elephants help central Africa's rainforests store more carbon: 26 to 60 more tonnes of biomass per hectare (Nature Geoscience).

pages.title: FreshWater Watch (Earthwatch Europe)
pages.desc: FreshWater Watch trains citizen scientists to test rivers, lakes and ponds: 80,000+ datasets from 22,000+ volunteers (organization figures).

pages.title: GCOM-C "SHIKISAI" (JAXA)
pages.desc: Japan's SHIKISAI satellite checks the health of Earth from space every 2 or 3 days, tracking clouds, aerosols, ocean color, plants, snow and ice (JAXA).

pages.title: GEDI Forest Lidar (NASA)
pages.desc: GEDI fires lasers from the International Space Station to measure the height and 3D shape of Earth's forests (University of Maryland).

pages.title: The GLOBE Program
pages.desc: A worldwide science program where students and citizen scientists collect real environmental data: more than 293 million measurements from 127 countries.

pages.title: GOES-19 and CCOR-1 (NOAA)
pages.desc: NOAA's GOES-19 carries CCOR-1, the world's first operational space-based coronagraph, imaging the Sun's corona every 15 minutes.

pages.title: GOSAT-GW "IBUKI GW" (JAXA)
pages.desc: JAXA's IBUKI GW tracks carbon dioxide, methane and nitrogen dioxide while also measuring the water cycle. Launched June 29, 2025 from Tanegashima Space Center.

pages.title: GRACE-FO (NASA / Germany)
pages.desc: Twin US-German satellites weigh Earth's water by measuring gravity, tracking groundwater, ice and sea level since 2018. Active.

pages.title: GSMaP Global Rainfall Map (JAXA)
pages.desc: JAXA's Global Satellite Mapping of Precipitation maps rain around the world every hour, used by 18,673 registered users in 163 countries and regions.

pages.title: Galileo Satellite Navigation (EU / ESA)
pages.desc: Europe's Galileo is the world's most precise satellite navigation system, serving over five billion smartphone users and helping rescues (ESA).

pages.title: GeoXO Geostationary Extended Observations (NOAA / NASA)
pages.desc: NOAA's next generation of geostationary weather satellites, planned from 2032, will improve warnings of severe weather and hazards (NOAA).

pages.title: Global Flood Awareness System (GloFAS)
pages.desc: Free global river flood forecasts up to 30 days ahead, plus 4-month outlooks, from the Copernicus Emergency Management Service.

pages.title: Global Fishing Watch
pages.desc: Global Fishing Watch uses satellites and SI to map fishing; its 2024 Nature study found about 75% of industrial fishing vessels are not publicly tracked.

pages.title: Global Forest Watch (WRI)
pages.desc: Free satellite forest data and deforestation alerts from WRI; where Indigenous forest monitors used it, deforestation fell 52% in one year.

pages.title: Globe at Night (NSF NOIRLab)
pages.desc: Globe at Night invites anyone to measure how dark their night sky is. People have sent 331,065 observations to track light pollution (program figures).

pages.title: Glossary
pages.desc: Simple definitions of the science words used across Saving Planets. On any solution page, tap or hover over a dotted word to see what it means.

pages.title: The Great Bubble Barrier
pages.desc: The Great Bubble Barrier's bubble curtain guides plastic out of Amsterdam's canals into a catchment across the full width and depth, while boats and fish pass.

pages.title: Great Green Wall (African Union / UNCCD)
pages.desc: An African-led effort to restore land across the Sahel. A 2020 UN status report counted about 4 million hectares restored inside the Great Green Wall zone.

pages.title: Great Lakes Plastic Cleanup
pages.desc: The Great Lakes Plastic Cleanup captures plastic across the world's largest freshwater system using Seabins, drones, and beach robots.

pages.title: Hayabusa2 Torifune Flyby (JAXA)
pages.desc: On 5 July 2026, JAXA's Hayabusa2 passed about 400 m above asteroid Torifune, the closest flyby of any Solar System body so far (JAXA).

pages.title: Heal the Bay
pages.desc: Since 1985, Heal the Bay has worked to make the coastal waters and watersheds of Greater Los Angeles safe, healthy and clean (Heal the Bay).

pages.title: Healthy Seas
pages.desc: Volunteer divers recover ghost nets: Healthy Seas reports 1,309.1 tons of nets and marine litter removed since 2013 (Healthy Seas figure).

pages.title: Hera
pages.desc: ESA's Hera arrives at the asteroid Dimorphos in November 2026 to measure what NASA's DART impact did, turning deflection into a repeatable defense.

pages.title: Hohmann Transfer Calculator
pages.desc: A Hohmann transfer moves a spacecraft between two circular orbits with two engine burns. Free on Saving Planets, with no ads on learning pages.

pages.title: Start Here: Homeschool Space and Flight Science, Ages 5–18
pages.desc: A free, no-sign-up path for homeschool families: what to use at each age, a 12-week plan from kids pages to high-school math, and a printable plan.

pages.title: HydroGNSS (ESA)
pages.desc: ESA's first Scout mission uses reflected navigation-satellite signals to measure soil moisture, wetlands and frozen ground (ESA).

pages.title: ICESat-2 (NASA)
pages.desc: NASA's ICESat-2 laser fires 10,000 pulses a second to measure ice sheets, sea ice, forests and coastal seafloor in 3D. Active.

pages.title: IMAP (NASA)
pages.desc: NASA's IMAP watches the Sun from about a million miles sunward and can give about a half hour's warning of incoming radiation.

pages.title: INSAT-3DS Weather Satellite (ISRO)
pages.desc: India's INSAT-3DS watches weather, land and oceans from geostationary orbit and carries a search-and-rescue transponder (ISRO).

pages.title: ISS Water Recovery: 98%
pages.desc: The space station now recycles 98% of the water its crews bring along, thanks to a Brine Processor Assembly, technology that matters wherever water is scarce.

pages.title: International Charter: Space and Major Disasters
pages.desc: When disaster strikes, 17 space agencies and satellite operators pool their satellites and give free images to rescue teams. Activated 1,000 times.

pages.title: International Coastal Cleanup (Ocean Conservancy)
pages.desc: Since 1986, more than 19 million volunteers have collected more than 400 million pounds of trash from beaches and waterways (Ocean Conservancy).

pages.title: Joint Polar Satellite System (NOAA)
pages.desc: NOAA's polar weather satellites circle Earth 14 times a day. Polar-orbiting satellites supply about 85% of the data used by weather prediction models.

pages.title: Juice (ESA)
pages.desc: ESA's Juice will study Ganymede, Callisto and Europa, with 35 moon flybys after it reaches Jupiter in July 2031. Cruising.

pages.title: Jupiter
pages.desc: Jupiter is a natural space debris removal system that swallows or flings away far more dangerous objects than any human mission could.

pages.title: Justdiggit
pages.desc: With farmers and pastoralists in Africa, Justdiggit is restoring 525,000 hectares of dry land and has brought back 32.3 million trees (organization figures).

pages.title: Keep Tahoe Blue (League to Save Lake Tahoe)
pages.desc: Keep Tahoe Blue, the League to Save Lake Tahoe, has protected the lake for decades, and its volunteers picked up 1,330 pounds of litter after July 4, 2026.

pages.title: Kelp Forests
pages.desc: Kelp can grow up to 18 inches a day, building underwater forests that feed and shelter thousands of species. Nature, studied and protected by NOAA and partners.

pages.title: Kids Planet Map
pages.desc: A playful map of our planet for kids: tap Oceans, Forests, Lakes, Rivers, Space and more to get a wow fact and real solutions that help people and nature.

pages.title: Kissimmee River Restoration (Florida)
pages.desc: Once straightened into a canal, Florida's Kissimmee River is winding again: 44 miles of river and 20,000 acres of wetlands restored (SFWMD).

pages.title: Klamath River Dam Removal
pages.desc: Four Klamath River dams came out by October 2024, reopening more than 400 miles of habitat to salmon, steelhead and lamprey (Klamath River Renewal).

pages.title: Lake Erie Harmful Algal Bloom Forecast (NOAA)
pages.desc: NOAA forecasts and tracks toxic algae in western Lake Erie through the summer so cities and swimmers can keep drinking water and people safe (NOAA NCCOS).

pages.title: Lake Plastic Recovery
pages.desc: Saving Planets' own lake solution: recover plastic from freshwater lakes by skimming, shoreline collection and divers, before it travels downstream to the sea.

pages.title: Lakes
pages.desc: Lake plastic recovery: pulling submerged litter from freshwater lakes, scuba divers, Great Lakes capture technology, and ROV deep-water cleanup.

pages.title: Landsat 9 (NASA / USGS)
pages.desc: Landsat 9 continues a 50-year record of Earth’s land, collecting 740 scenes a day and, with Landsat 8, seeing each place every 8 days.

pages.title: Learn
pages.desc: Free lessons from kids to PhD in three tracks: orbital mechanics, aeronautical engineering and physics. The math is taught inside each track, step by step.

pages.title: LeoLabs
pages.desc: LeoLabs runs a global network of ground radars that track satellites and debris in low Earth orbit and turn the data into collision warnings.

pages.title: Lesson Plan Builder
pages.desc: Free printable lesson plans for K-3 to university, built from real environmental and space solutions that help both people and nature.

pages.title: Libera Earth Energy Instrument (NASA)
pages.desc: Libera will measure how much energy leaves Earth each day, keeping a climate record that began in 2000 going strong (NOAA).

pages.title: Life Terra
pages.desc: Life Terra and its partners have planted more than 36 million trees across Europe (company figure), working toward a goal of 500 million trees.

pages.title: Lift Equation Calculator
pages.desc: The lift equation says how much upward force a wing makes: twice as fast means four times the lift. Free on Saving Planets, with no ads on learning pages.

pages.title: LignoSat Wooden Satellite (Kyoto University)
pages.desc: LignoSat, the world's first wooden satellite, proved wood can survive in orbit; a follow-on is a potential solution on the horizon.

pages.title: Living Lakes (Global Nature Fund)
pages.desc: Since 1998, the Global Nature Fund's Living Lakes Network has protected and restored lakes and wetlands with 130 member organizations in more than 60 countries.

pages.title: Living Lands & Waters
pages.desc: A barge-based river cleanup crew that, with more than 141,000 volunteers, has pulled over 14 million pounds of trash from U.S. rivers.

pages.title: London Tideway Tunnel (Super Sewer)
pages.desc: London's new super sewer catches sewage that used to spill into the River Thames in storms, with room for 1.6 million cubic metres (Tideway).

pages.title: Lucy (NASA)
pages.desc: NASA's Lucy is touring asteroids; after Dinkinesh and Donaldjohanson, it reaches its first Trojan asteroid, Eurybates, on 11 August 2027 (NASA).

pages.title: MMX
pages.desc: JAXA's MMX launches October 2026 to land on Mars's moon Phobos and return at least 10 grams of it to Earth in 2031, a first for the Mars system.

pages.title: Mach Number & Speed of Sound Calculator (Standard Atmosphere)
pages.desc: The speed of sound depends only on air temperature, so it falls as you climb to about 11 km. The Mach number is your speed divided by the local speed of sound.

pages.title: Mangrove Forests
pages.desc: About 80 species of mangrove trees guard tropical coastlines: their tangled roots hold mud in place, soften storm surges and give fish food and shelter.

pages.title: MetOp-SG-A1 and Sentinel-5A
pages.desc: Launched August 2025 on Ariane 6, MetOp-SG-A1 carries Sentinel-5, which delivers daily global data on air pollutants, ozone and climate gases.

pages.title: Meteosat Third Generation (ESA / EUMETSAT)
pages.desc: Three weather satellites now watch Europe and Africa from 36,000 km up, with new images every 2.5 minutes and a camera that catches lightning day and night.

pages.title: Mission Blue Hope Spots
pages.desc: Founded by ocean scientist Dr. Sylvia Earle, Mission Blue backs a community-led network of 168 Hope Spots, ocean places local champions work to protect.

pages.title: The Moon Steadies Earth’s Tilt
pages.desc: Saving moons, saving planets: the Moon keeps Earth's 23.5-degree tilt in check, which keeps our seasons and climate stable (NASA).

pages.title: Mote Marine Laboratory
pages.desc: Mote scientists have restored more than 216,000 corals to Florida's Coral Reef, and their restored corals now spawn (Mote figure).

pages.title: Mr. Trash Wheel Family
pages.desc: Baltimore's Trash Wheels intercept about 500 tons of trash a year before it reaches the harbor and the Chesapeake Bay (organization figure).

pages.title: Myth or Fact? Evidence Arcade
pages.desc: A free true-or-false game for kids built from Saving Planets Myth vs Fact and Amazing Facts. Every answer shows its real source. No timer, no sign-up.

pages.title: Myth vs Fact
pages.desc: Common doom myths about Earth and space, each checked against a NASA, NOAA or ESA source. Hopeful where the evidence is, honest where the work isn't done.

pages.title: NEO Surveyor
pages.desc: NASA NEO Surveyor is the first space telescope built to find hazardous asteroids, including dark ones hidden in the Sun's glare. Launch NET September 2027.

pages.title: NISAR (NASA–ISRO)
pages.desc: NISAR, a NASA and ISRO radar satellite launched from India on July 30, 2025, scans nearly all of Earth's land and ice twice every 12 days, even through clouds.

pages.title: Namami Gange (India)
pages.desc: India's Namami Gange programme has created or rehabilitated 4,263 million litres a day of sewage treatment for the River Ganga (government figures).

pages.title: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope (NASA)
pages.desc: NASA's Roman telescope launched Aug 30, 2026 to L2: Hubble-sharp images 100x wider, a census of planetary systems, first images by early 2027.

pages.title: OCO-2 Orbiting Carbon Observatory (NASA)
pages.desc: NASA's OCO-2 satellite has measured carbon dioxide around the planet since 2014, showing where carbon is released and where forests and oceans absorb it.

pages.title: OSIRIS-APEX and Apophis 2029 (NASA)
pages.desc: On April 13, 2029, asteroid Apophis passes about 20,000 miles from Earth. NASA's OSIRIS-APEX meets it in June 2029 to see how that close pass changes it.

pages.title: The Ocean Cleanup
pages.desc: The Ocean Cleanup removes legacy plastic from ocean garbage patches and intercepts it in rivers: more than 65 million kilograms caught as of October 2026.

pages.title: Ocean Voyages Institute
pages.desc: A sailing nonprofit that has pulled more than 850,000 pounds of plastic from the Pacific Gyre in 10 voyages (nonprofit figure).

pages.title: Oceans
pages.desc: Ocean solutions that are working now: The Ocean Cleanup's systems and river Interceptors, 4ocean's cleanup crews, and Plastic Bank's recycling economy.

pages.title: One Tree Planted
pages.desc: Since 2014, One Tree Planted has planted more than 171 million trees with 489 partners in 84 countries (organization figure).

pages.title: OpenET Satellite Water Data
pages.desc: Free satellite data on how much water crops and land use, now for all 48 contiguous states, with more than 13,000 registered users.

pages.title: Orbit Lab
pages.desc: Interactive Orbit Lab: plan a Hohmann transfer or altitude raise around Earth with real vis-viva physics, animated and accessible, in 5 languages.

pages.title: Orbital Mechanics Math, Step by Step
pages.desc: From your first orbit equation to Lambert’s problem: derivations, worked examples and practice problems, freshman to PhD, free and in five languages.

pages.title: Orbital Data Centers
pages.desc: Data centers in orbit run SI chips on solar power and radiate waste heat into space, with no water-cooling towers. Early flights only, not yet a replacement.

pages.title: Orbital Period Calculator
pages.desc: The orbital period is how long a satellite takes to go once around the Earth. Circular orbit around a spherical Earth; no drag or J2.

pages.title: Orbital Velocity & Escape Velocity Calculator
pages.desc: Orbital velocity is the speed needed to stay in a circular orbit at a given height. Spherical Earth, no air drag, no Earth rotation bonus.

pages.title: Orbits Explained
pages.desc: Why satellites don’t fall down, how fast they go, and how rockets change orbits, in plain language for kids, teens and college students.

pages.title: PACE (NASA)
pages.desc: NASA's PACE reads the color of the ocean to track phytoplankton, the base of the marine food web, plus aerosols and clouds.

pages.title: PREFIRE Polar CubeSats (NASA)
pages.desc: Two shoebox-size NASA satellites measure the far-infrared heat that Earth's poles send into space (NASA JPL). Last reviewed: October 2026 · 4 sources cited

pages.title: PRELUDE (ClearSpace)
pages.desc: PRELUDE is a ClearSpace and ESA mission planned for June 2027 to validate close-proximity rendezvous technology. A potential solution on the horizon.

pages.title: PUNCH (NASA)
pages.desc: Four suitcase-sized NASA satellites image the Sun's corona and solar wind together, in 3D, since March 2025. Active in low Earth orbit.

pages.title: Pan-STARRS Near-Earth Object Search
pages.desc: Two telescopes on Haleakalā, Maui, that in 2021 found nearly as many near-Earth objects as the rest of the world's observatories combined.

pages.title: Parker Solar Probe (NASA)
pages.desc: The first spacecraft to fly through the Sun's outer atmosphere, helping scientists understand the space weather that affects life and technology on Earth.

pages.title: Pendulum Period Calculator (Small and Large Angles)
pages.desc: A pendulum’s period is the time for one full swing there and back. Simple pendulum: point mass, light rigid string, no friction, standard gravity 9.80665 m/s².

pages.title: Penobscot River Restoration (Maine)
pages.desc: After two dams came out of Maine's Penobscot River, nearly 5.93 million river herring climbed the Milford fish lift in 2025, up from about 590,000 in 2015.

pages.title: Physics Explained
pages.desc: Physics for kids, teens and college students: forces and collisions, air resistance, pendulums, magnetism and auroras, heat, and relativity in GPS.

pages.title: Physics Lab
pages.desc: Interactive Physics Lab: projectile with quadratic drag (RK4), damped oscillator with eigenvalues and response plot, and exact pendulum period, in 5 languages.

pages.title: Physics, step by step
pages.desc: Mechanics, drag, oscillations, Lagrangians, electromagnetism, thermodynamics, fluids and GPS relativity: derivations and worked examples, college to PhD.

pages.title: Phytoplankton, the Ocean's Oxygen Engine
pages.desc: Tiny ocean plants produce about half of Earth's oxygen, making phytoplankton one of the planet's most important natural systems.

pages.title: Planetary Defense
pages.desc: Planetary defense solutions: ESA Hera at the asteroid DART moved, NASA NEO Surveyor, Webb and asteroid 2024 YR4, and Jupiter, the natural shield.

pages.title: Plant-for-the-Planet
pages.desc: Started by a 9-year-old in 2007, Plant-for-the-Planet trains young Climate Justice Ambassadors and restores forests, including Mexico's Mayan forests.

pages.title: Plastic Bank
pages.desc: Plastic Bank pays collectors in vulnerable communities to gather ocean-bound plastic, exchanged at local branches for income, food vouchers and school supplies.

pages.title: Plastic Odyssey
pages.desc: Plastic Odyssey sets up small recycling factories in places with no recycling system, turning plastic waste into useful products and local jobs.

pages.title: Plato (ESA)
pages.desc: ESA's Plato will use 26 cameras to hunt for Earth-like planets around Sun-like stars, with launch planned for March 2027 on Ariane 6.

pages.title: Play & Learn
pages.desc: Kids games and activities about our planet: Kids Planet Map, Spot the Fire from Space, Satellite Explorer, Amazing Facts, Myth vs Fact and the Glossary.

pages.title: Polar
pages.desc: Satellites that watch the ice of Antarctica, the Arctic, Greenland and Iceland, from sea-ice thickness to hidden lakes under the ice sheets.

pages.title: Posidonia Seagrass Meadows
pages.desc: The Mediterranean seagrass Posidonia oceanica forms meadows that are thousands of years old and store carbon in the seafloor (CEAB-CSIC).

pages.title: Press and Media
pages.desc: Press and media kit for Saving Planets: logo downloads, mission, boilerplate, contact and fact sheets. Everything you need to write about Saving Planets.

pages.title: Privacy Policy
pages.desc: What we collect, why, and how you stay in control. Short version: very little, and nothing without your OK. We do not sell or share personal information.

pages.title: Project Rawane
pages.desc: Project R: the two-way relationship between Earth and space — how space work protects the planet and planetary work keeps space worth protecting.

pages.title: Project Seagrass
pages.desc: Project Seagrass, a UK charity, has planted more than 150,000 seagrass seeds to bring back underwater meadows (organization figures).

pages.title: Projectile Motion Calculator with Air Resistance
pages.desc: Real balls do not follow a perfect parabola: air drag shortens the range and lowers the peak. A free projectile motion calculator with air resistance.

pages.title: Psyche (NASA)
pages.desc: NASA's Psyche used a Mars flyby on 15 May 2026 to head for a metal-rich asteroid it will orbit from August 2029, to learn what a planet's core is like.

pages.title: RADARSAT Constellation Mission (Canada)
pages.desc: Three Canadian radar satellites watch Canada's land, coasts and Arctic day and night, through cloud and smoke, with about 250,000 images a year.

pages.title: Rainforest Connection
pages.desc: Solar-powered Guardian listening devices and SI detect chainsaws in real time; Rainforest Connection reports more than 726,000 hectares of rainforest protected.

pages.title: Ramses (ESA / JAXA)
pages.desc: ESA and JAXA's Ramses must launch by spring 2028 to meet Apophis before its 2029 Earth pass. Its €81.2 million build contract was signed in February 2026.

pages.title: Rawane's Mission Log
pages.desc: Rawane's Mission Log: short weekly story posts from the Saving Planets astronaut mascot, tied to real solutions with every fact sourced and linked.

pages.title: Restoring the Lake Depths Foundation
pages.desc: A Nevada nonprofit whose ROVs and volunteer divers pull submerged trash from Lake Tahoe, from the surface down to 1,640 feet: over 13 tons in summer 2024 alone.

pages.title: Rewilding Europe
pages.desc: Rewilding Europe helps wild nature come back across Europe. Rewilding Europe, working with local partners in large pioneering landscapes.

pages.title: River Cleanup
pages.desc: River Cleanup and its volunteers have recovered more than 4.39 million kg of waste from rivers worldwide and aim for 1,000 plastic-free rivers by 2050.

pages.title: Rivers
pages.desc: River interceptors catch plastic in the rivers that carry most of it to the ocean. Each solution page lists its own sourced figures.

pages.title: Rotor Hover Power Calculator (Momentum Theory)
pages.desc: A hovering helicopter or drone pushes air down to hold itself up. Free on Saving Planets, with no ads on learning pages.

pages.title: SARSAT Search and Rescue Satellites (NOAA)
pages.desc: NOAA's SARSAT satellites relay distress beacon signals to rescuers; the international system has supported more than 50,000 rescues worldwide since 1982 (NOAA).

pages.title: How SI Helper works and what we don’t keep
pages.desc: How the SI Helper pilot on the Teachers page answers from Saving Planets pages only, its safety checks and limits, and what it does not keep.

pages.title: SMAP Soil Moisture Active Passive (NASA)
pages.desc: SMAP maps the water in Earth's soil from space, helping improve predictions of weather, floods and droughts (NASA).

pages.title: SOHO Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (ESA / NASA)
pages.desc: Watching the Sun nonstop since 1995, SOHO helps experts predict solar storms and has found more than 5,000 comets (NASA).

pages.title: SOLAR-1 (NOAA)
pages.desc: NOAA's SOLAR-1 (formerly SWFO-L1) watches the Sun from L1, about one million miles from Earth, streaming space weather data to forecasters in real time.

pages.title: SPHEREx (NASA)
pages.desc: Launched 11 March 2025, NASA's SPHEREx maps the whole sky in 102 infrared colors and finished its first all-sky map in 2025 (NASA JPL).

pages.title: SWOT (NASA–CNES)
pages.desc: SWOT measures more than 95% of Earth's lakes larger than 15 acres and rivers wider than 330 feet, the first global survey of fresh water.

pages.title: Saharan Dust Feeds the Amazon
pages.desc: Every year about 27.7 million tons of Saharan dust falls on the Amazon, delivering some 22,000 tons of phosphorus that the rainforest needs (NASA).

pages.title: Salt Marshes
pages.desc: Salt marshes are nurseries for more than 75% of fisheries species and buffer shorelines from erosion and floods (NOAA). Twice a day with the tides, all year.

pages.title: Satellite Explorer
pages.desc: An interactive satellite explorer: drag the parts of a satellite into place, then learn about laser links and computing in orbit, from K-3 to university.

pages.title: SeaTrees
pages.desc: SeaTrees connects people with local partners restoring mangroves, coral reefs, kelp forests and seagrass meadows around the world (SeaTrees).

pages.title: Sea Turtle Conservancy
pages.desc: Sea Turtle Conservancy works in 8 countries, has tagged and monitored more than 550 turtles and trained over 1,200 researchers (nonprofit figures).

pages.title: Seabin
pages.desc: Seabin's floating bins have captured 33.0 million items in Sydney Harbour since 2020, including 18.9 million microplastics (company figures).

pages.title: Seagrass Meadows
pages.desc: Seagrass covers just 0.1% of the seafloor but stores 11% of the ocean's buried organic carbon, and one acre can support almost 40,000 fish, NOAA says.

pages.title: Copernicus Sentinel-1 (ESA)
pages.desc: Sentinel-1 radar sees through clouds, day and night, to map floods, earthquakes and ice; Sentinel-1C and 1D joined in 2024 and 2025.

pages.title: Copernicus Sentinel-2C (ESA)
pages.desc: Sentinel-2C joined the Copernicus fleet in September 2024, imaging land and coasts in 13 bands so forests and crops are checked every five days.

pages.title: Copernicus Sentinel-3 (ESA / EUMETSAT)
pages.desc: The Copernicus Sentinel-3 satellites measure Earth's oceans, land, ice and atmosphere, and a third satellite, Sentinel-3C, launched on September 15, 2026 (ESA).

pages.title: Copernicus Sentinel-4 (ESA / EUMETSAT)
pages.desc: From geostationary orbit on MTG-S1, Sentinel-4 measures air pollution such as nitrogen dioxide and ozone over Europe and North Africa every hour (ESA).

pages.title: Copernicus Sentinel-5P (ESA)
pages.desc: Copernicus Sentinel-5P maps the gases in the air we breathe, covering the whole planet every day with its Tropomi instrument (ESA).

pages.title: Copernicus Sentinel-6B (ESA / NASA)
pages.desc: Sentinel-6B, launched November 17, 2025, continues the precise record of global sea level that began in the early 1990s.

pages.title: Site Map
pages.desc: Every hub and solution on Saving Planets in one list, from oceans, lakes, rivers and forests to space and Earth observation, so you can find any page fast.

pages.title: Solar Orbiter (ESA / NASA)
pages.desc: ESA and NASA's Solar Orbiter took the first close-up images of the Sun's poles, coming within 42 million km of the Sun. Active, orbiting the Sun.

pages.title: 191 Real Solutions Making a Difference Daily
pages.desc: Proof it's not too late: 191 real, sourced solutions across 11 hubs, from ocean cleanups to Earth-observation satellites, making a difference daily.

pages.title: Space
pages.desc: Space is part of Earth’s environment. Solutions for orbit: active debris removal, sustainable in-orbit servicing and orbital data centers, each with sources.

pages.title: Northrop Grumman SpaceLogistics
pages.desc: Life extension in GEO: two MEVs have docked with three satellites, and the Mission Robotic Vehicle and three pods launched July 21, 2026 (company figures).

pages.title: Space Disposal
pages.desc: Space Disposal: the missions that capture and remove legacy debris from orbit, led by Astroscale's ADRAS-J2 for JAXA, with a source for every figure.

pages.title: Space Passport
pages.desc: A free Space Passport for kids: collect stamps for exploring oceans, forests, space weather, planetary defense and more. Saved only on your device.

pages.title: Space Weather & Shields
pages.desc: Space Weather & Shields: the heliosphere, magnetosphere and ozone layer, plus NOAA SOLAR-1, ESA Vigil and ISRO Aditya-L1 watching the Sun to protect Earth.

pages.title: Spot the Fire from Space: How big is a pixel?
pages.desc: A free astroEDU-format classroom activity: students lay coarse and fine grids over a paper landscape to see why pixel size matters for spotting wildfires.

pages.title: Stall Speed Calculator (with Bank Angle and Altitude)
pages.desc: Stall speed is the slowest a wing can fly while still holding the aircraft up. Generic aircraft, steady flight, U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976.

pages.title: Starfish Space Otter
pages.desc: The first Otter launched October 1, 2026 for NASA's SSPICY mission, inspecting up to four dead satellites and rocket bodies from 2027.

pages.title: Sungai Watch
pages.desc: Sungai Watch stops plastic in Indonesian rivers with trash barriers, daily collection and sorting, plus upcycling, working in Bali and Java since 2020.

pages.title: Surfrider Foundation
pages.desc: Surfrider Foundation volunteers protect the ocean, waves and beaches, and in 2025 they removed 338,383 pounds of trash from U.S. coasts (Surfrider).

pages.title: TEMPO Air Quality Mission (NASA)
pages.desc: From geostationary orbit, NASA's TEMPO measures air pollution over North America every daylight hour, a first from space (NASA).

pages.title: TRACERS (NASA)
pages.desc: NASA's twin TRACERS satellites fly through Earth's polar cusps to study magnetic reconnection, a key driver of space weather.

pages.title: Tanager-1 (Carbon Mapper / Planet)
pages.desc: Tanager-1, built by Planet with a NASA JPL-designed spectrometer for the nonprofit Carbon Mapper, pinpoints methane and CO2 plumes from single sources.

pages.title: Teacher Sheets
pages.desc: A printable one-page sheet for every Saving Planets solution: the Five W's, a kid-friendly summary, sources and three discussion questions.

pages.title: Terraformation
pages.desc: Terraformation grows native, biodiverse forests from seed to canopy across the tropics and Hawaii, funding seed collection, nurseries, planting and monitoring.

pages.title: The SeaCleaners
pages.desc: Mobula cleanup boats catch plastic close to where it starts, and in Malaysia one boat turned 135,000 pieces of debris into community walkways (The SeaCleaners).

pages.title: Three Invisible Shields
pages.desc: Three natural shields protect Earth: the heliosphere, the magnetosphere, and the atmosphere with its ozone layer, deflecting solar wind and most harmful UV-B.

pages.title: Three Trees for Every One Removed
pages.desc: Saving Planets' own forest rule: plant three trees for every one removed, so each removal becomes a net gain for habitat, soil and shade, and is easy to verify.

pages.title: Thrust-to-Weight Ratio Calculator
pages.desc: The thrust-to-weight ratio compares an engine’s push with the vehicle’s weight. Liftoff instant, vertical flight, no drag.

pages.title: Titan
pages.desc: Titan is a prebiotic time capsule, and NASA's Dragonfly rotorcraft explores it from 2034, building radar, power and autonomy tools that matter for Earth.

pages.title: This Week's Saving Planets Top Ten Features
pages.desc: This week's top ten on Saving Planets: 191 real solutions, Myth vs Fact, the Weekly Brief, lessons from kids to PhD, the World Map, Roman and the new Polar hub.

pages.title: Topics A to Z
pages.desc: Every solution, hub and science word on Saving Planets, from A to Z: oceans, lakes, rivers, forests, space, Earth observation and the glossary terms.

pages.title: Trees for the Future
pages.desc: Partnering with East African farmers on regenerative farms: 450M+ trees grown and 99,000 acres restored (nonprofit figures).

pages.title: Trout Unlimited
pages.desc: Trout Unlimited restores and reconnects cold, clean rivers, reconnecting 1,052 miles of streams in its 2024-25 season (Trout Unlimited).

pages.title: The Science of Tsunami Detection
pages.desc: Deep-ocean buoys, satellites, GPS signals and seafloor cables spot tsunamis in the open ocean so coastal communities get time to reach high ground (NOAA, NASA).

pages.title: Methane Alert and Response System (UNEP)
pages.desc: The UN's satellite methane alert system has sent more than 3,500 alerts about major leaks in 33 countries, and responses rose from 1% to 12% in a year.

pages.title: U.S. Deorbit Vehicle (NASA / SpaceX)
pages.desc: NASA selected SpaceX to build the U.S. Deorbit Vehicle that will guide the International Space Station safely out of orbit after 2030.

pages.title: Veggie Space Garden (NASA)
pages.desc: NASA's Veggie garden grows fresh food on the International Space Station; in 2015 astronauts ate the first lettuce grown in it (NASA).

pages.title: Vigil (ESA)
pages.desc: ESA's Vigil will watch the Sun from L5, giving up to four to five days' notice of certain space weather effects. Launch is planned for 2031.

pages.title: Voyager 1 and 2 (NASA)
pages.desc: Launched in 1977, the twin Voyagers are in interstellar space, and on Nov. 18, 2026, Voyager 1 will be one light-day from Earth (NASA).

pages.title: Waterkeeper Alliance
pages.desc: Waterkeeper Alliance unites hundreds of local Waterkeeper groups that patrol and protect more than 6 million square miles of rivers, lakes and coastlines.

pages.title: Ways to Help
pages.desc: Give to, or join, the people doing the work, from ocean and river cleanups to tree planting. Saving Planets doesn’t take donations or receive any of the money.

pages.title: WeForest
pages.desc: WeForest has grown more than 118 million trees and has 100,000 hectares of forest under restoration and conservation (WeForest).

pages.title: Webb and 2024 YR4
pages.desc: How the James Webb Space Telescope tracked asteroid 2024 YR4 in February 2026 and ruled out a 2032 Moon impact, two years before ground telescopes could.

pages.title: Whales, Ocean Gardeners
pages.desc: Whale waste carries nutrients to the ocean surface and fertilizes phytoplankton, the tiny plants at the base of the ocean food web (NOAA Fisheries).

pages.title: Our 191 solutions around the world
pages.desc: An interactive world map of every Saving Planets solution: green pins are working now, blue pins are coming soon, and rocket pins show upcoming launches.

pages.title: Yellowstone Wolves
pages.desc: Gray wolves returned to Yellowstone in 1995 after nearly 70 years; in January 2026 at least 84 lived in the park, in eight packs (NPS).

pages.title: Zero Debris Charter (ESA)
pages.desc: The Zero Debris Charter sets shared targets to stop creating space debris by 2030; by May 2026 it had 228 signatories from 34 countries (ESA).

pages.title: Welcome to Saving Our Planet Minus the DOOM
pages.desc: Practical, sourced solutions for oceans, lakes, rivers, forests and space, plus computing that does not drink the planet dry. Positive action, not panic.
